content:
## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `addpipe32` (32-bit registered adder: y = a + b (mod 2^32)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;

        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= a_i + b_i;
    end
end

endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 671.384 um^2, WNS 7.57073 ns, estimated score 75.035916 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: I'll start by trying an explicit Kogge-Stone prefix adder, since timing dominates the score (10×WNS vs 0.001×area).
Timing floor (no logic) is ~7.89, so the whole adder only costs ~0.32 ns. Let me probe a couple of architectures.
Ripple confirms ~0.069 ns/level, so ABC's flat adder (~0.32 ns total) is already near-optimal depth. Let me probe restructuring of the reset/enable logic off the sum path.
Yosys's `$add` likely uses an OR-propagate lookahead. Let me try prefix trees using T=a|b (cheaper/faster than XOR) in the carry tree.
Idea: move the final XOR and enable-mux off the carry path (select the flop input with the carry). Testing two versions.

All structural alternatives (Kogge-Stone, Sklansky, Han-Carlson, carry-select, OR-propagate trees, output-mux carry-select, subtract form) estimate 0.05–0.3 ns *slower* than the flow's own `+` mapping, and since the score is dominated by 10×WNS (area is only 0.001/µm²), none of them can win: e.g. Sklansky saves 130 µm² (+0.13) but loses 0.06 ns (−0.6).

Measurement summary (estimates):

| variant | area | WNS | est. score |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain `+` (best) | 671.4 | 7.5707 | 75.04 |
| Kogge-Stone | 625.4 | 7.4990 | 74.36 |
| Sklansky | 539.7 | 7.5073 | 74.53 |
| Sklansky + reset/enable off sum path | 533.3 | 7.5232 | 74.70 |
| carry-select 2×16 / 4×8 | 644/638 | 7.393/7.260 | 73.3/72.0 |
| explicit ripple | 417.1 | 5.6833 | 56.4 |
| no-logic floor (`y<=a_i`) | 247.6 | 7.8878 | — |

The floor with zero adder logic is 7.888 ns, so the whole 32-bit adder only costs ~0.32 ns ≈ 5–6 cell levels — already at the practical depth limit for this library, which is why no hand-built prefix network beats it. The verified place-and-route run of the best form scored **74.156** (area 746.13 µm², WNS 7.49026 ns).

input.summary: I characterized the timing budget first: a logic-free version (y_o <= a_i) reaches WNS 7.888 ns, so the entire 32-bit adder plus enable/reset logic only costs ~0.32 ns (~5-6 cell levels), while area is worth only 0.001 pt/um^2 versus 10 pt/ns. I then probed many adder architectures with estimate_ppa: Kogge-Stone (7.499), Sklansky (7.507), Han-Carlson (7.404), Sklansky/KS with OR-propagate (7.512/7.501), carry-select 2x16 and 4x8 (7.393/7.260), explicit ripple (5.683), subtract-form add (7.510), plus restructurings that pull the synchronous reset and the valid enable off the sum path and even select the flop data with the carry (7.487-7.560). Every alternative was slower than the flow's native `+` mapping (7.5707 ns, 671 um^2), and the area savings (up to 150 um^2 = 0.15 pt) never compensated the 0.05-0.3 ns timing loss (0.5-3 pt). The native mapping is therefore already at the depth limit for Nangate45 here, and I submitted it to place-and-route, verifying a score of 74.156 (area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.49026 ns). Three P&R submissions were left unused because no candidate had a credible chance of beating it.
